_README: EXPECTED-RED LEDGER. Every gate that is RED must appear here with a
MEASURED watermark, an owner and a review_by date. This is what lets CI
ask 'is anything red that we did not already record, or REDDER than we
recorded?' instead of 'is anything red?', which was a constant and
This ledger SOFTENS NOTHING. The gates still print RED, first, on every
run. What it changes is the exit code, so a NEW break is distinguishable
- a RED gate not listed here      -> FAIL (it is new)
- a RED gate worse than watermark -> FAIL (it regressed)
- a GREEN gate still listed here  -> FAIL (stale; delete the entry)
- past review_by                  -> FAIL (re-measure or sign an extension)
review_by is the anti-wallpaper clause: an expected-red gate must not

why_red: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-22 on a COMPLETE campaign. The previous watermark
(17.6%, 3 of 17) came from a run an operator power decision stopped at
N=17 of an intended 25; this one finished.
THIS IS NOT AN IMPROVEMENT CLAIM. 5/23 against 3/17 is within noise at
this sample size, and the layer fixes landed since the archived campaign
did NOT move the settled rate in any way this evidence can distinguish.
At N=17 the re-run reproduced the archived figures EXACTLY -- 15/17
ran-to-budget and 3 settled -- which is the strongest statement available
here: same population, same rates, no measurable change.
The watermark moves to the completed measurement because a finished N=25
is better evidence than an interrupted N=17, and because a watermark is a
regression floor: 21.7% is the harder number to hold and therefore the
honest one to record. Nothing here softens the bar, which remains >= 95%
of 200 hulls and is 4.4x away.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY FAILING: 16 of the 18 unsettled cases fail on TOTAL
drift and 2 on pressure. On the archived force histories the same
population reads viscous drift 0.00-0.67% in EVERY one of 16 hulls while
pressure drifts 3.08-21.82%, and the total simply tracks pressure. That
is `docs/research/CFD.md` section 2's KCS finding reproduced on a
population with nothing to do with KCS: the viscous half is right every
time and the pressure half is what does not settle. Chasing the settled
rate means chasing the pressure integral, not the mesh.
CLEARING CONDITION unchanged: >= 95% of a 200-hull batch meshing AND
settling unattended.

why_red: GAP G4, AND IT IS GAP D11's SHAPE FOUND A SECOND TIME. Until
2026-08-11 this clause had no row that could fail. Gate 6M printed
GREEN because tests/test_manufacturing.py PASSES -- and one of the
things it passes is
test_gate6_refold_clause_is_red_on_the_hull, which asserts
`db.max() > REFOLD_BAR_MM and dt.max() > REFOLD_BAR_MM`. The suite is
green BECAUSE the bar is missed. That test is honest and it stays; what
it is not is a VERDICT. Outside it the only statement of the shortfall
was one sentence in ALIGNMENT.md's STEP/IGES/DXF row -- prose, in a
document, with no owner and no expiry, which is exactly the state gap
D11 recorded for the generative feasibility clause before it became
Gate 4F.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, and it is geometry rather than tolerance. Until
2026-08-11 `hull_panels` took its rulings at CONSTANT STATION x, so the
ruling direction r lay in the y-z plane and det(A', r, r') collapsed to
A'_x (r x r')_x, which vanishes only where the section shape stops
changing. That is why the AFT HALF of the bottom panel -- flat keel,
constant deadrise, i.e. a PLANE -- refolded to 0.008 mm while the
forefoot, where the deadrise warps 8 deg to 30 deg, refolded 141.0 mm off.
THE CLEARING CONDITION WAS ATTEMPTED IN FULL AND IT IS NOT SUFFICIENT.
`unroll.developable_pairing` now solves for SLANTED rulings: the ruling
from keel station i lands at chine parameter v[i] != x[i], v is PINNED at
both ends so the panel still spans the whole edge, and the interior is
solved by Levenberg-Marquardt on the per-quad planarity condition with a
lambda ladder and a multigrid in the station count. It is deterministic
from the identity start and costs 0.63 s for both panels. WHAT IT BOUGHT,
worst panel, reference hull, 41 stations: 224.5 -> 66.2 mm two-sided,
225.7 -> 66.2 mm edge-only. A 3.4x improvement against a bar that is still
missed by 13x.
THREE MECHANISMS HOLD THE REST AND NOT ONE OF THEM IS A RULING CHOICE. (a)
NO EXACT DEVELOPABLE SPANS THE BOTTOM PANEL'S TWO EDGES. Marching the
planar-quad condition forward from the transom TERMINATES at keel x = 7.25
m of 10.00: no plane through the current ruling meets the chine ahead. The
fit can still reach machine-zero warp with both ends pinned -- by putting
1.846 m of chine, 7.4x the mean station spacing, into ONE quad whose chord
then misses the chine by 97.5 mm. (b) THE SHEER POLYLINE IS ALREADY 65.6
mm OFF THE SHEER CURVE at 41 stations, before developability is asked
about, converging at about O(h^0.5): 81.0 / 65.6 / 47.3 / 29.9 mm at 21 /
41 / 81 / 161 stations. `y_sheer = ys * w**0.15` drives dy/dx to infinity
at the stem. That is the floor the 66.2 mm topside sits on and it is a
GRAMMAR property. The chine, whose plan-form carries no such exponent,
reads 3.4 mm at the same 41 stations. (c) THE CHINE AND SHEER HAVE A SLOPE
DISCONTINUITY at x = x_mb * L (5.50 m here), where the plan-form exponent
switches branches and dw/dx jumps 0.1364 -> 0. The fitted topside refolds
to 0.69-0.92 mm aft of that crease and steps to 6.02-6.16 mm at exactly
that station and stays there, so the crease costs a 6 mm floor on its own
-- larger than the whole bar.
THE METRIC WAS MADE STRICTER, NOT LOOSER, IN THE SAME CHANGE. The
watermark used to be the edge-only `refold_deviation_mm`, and case (a)
above is that metric being BOUGHT: the uncapped fit reads 0.07 mm on it
with the panel 97.5 mm off the hull, and a ONE-SIDED panel-to-hull test
scores it perfect too, because every point of that chord lies between keel
and chine and is therefore ON the hull surface.
`refold_surface_deviation_mm` is two-sided and is now the watermark; the
constant-x control is re-measured under it (224.5) so the improvement
cannot be an artefact of the change. tests/test_manufacturing.py::test_the
_edge_only_refold_can_be_bought_and_the_ two_sided_one_cannot fires that
guard by removing the bound, and
::test_the_constant_x_control_is_worse_on_both_panels_and_both_metrics
runs the verbatim old ruling selection through the same measurement.
WHAT DID NOT WORK, recorded so it is not retried. (1) Letting BOTH edges
be reparametrised reached 30.4 mm on the topside but only from a random
start (44.6 mm from the identity), cost 16-18 s per panel against 0.63,
and was not reproducible -- shipped as single-edge. (2) A cubic spline
through the 41 stations, used before `Hull.edge_curves` existed, is itself
94.95 mm off the analytic sheer, so the first fits were measured against
the wrong hull; the closed form is now evaluated directly at the fitted
parameters. (3) An acceptance guard comparing max |quad_warp| instead of
the gate's own metric accepted a fit that was 1938 mm off on a rejection-
sampled hull at 161 stations against 612 mm for the constant-x family it
replaced -- a guard that watches a proxy passes the case the proxy cannot
see. (4) Bounding the ruling step to 2.0x the mean spacing costs the worst
panel 66.2 -> 93.6 mm; uncapping it costs 66.2 -> 97.5. `_MAX_RULING_STEP`
= 4.0 is CALIBRATED over three hulls and two station counts, not derived,
and the code says so.
IT STILL DOES NOT REFINE AWAY, on either ruling family: at 161 stations
the fitted panels read 64.1 / 102.2 mm and the constant-x control 143.1 /
203.4. tests/test_manufacturing.py::test_refold_does_not_converge_with_sta
tion_count pins both.
THE BAR IS NOT SOFTENED. REFOLD_BAR_MM is still 5.0, declared once in
tests/test_manufacturing.py, and both panels and every station are still
measured. This entry's `bar` field points AT that constant rather than
restating it.
NEXT, AND IT IS NOT MORE UNROLLER WORK. (b) and (c) are properties of
`geometry.station_geometry`: the `w**0.15` sheer envelope and the fore/aft
plan-form branch switch at x_mb. Clearing 5 mm needs a sheer taper with
bounded dy/dx at the stem and a C1 join at x_mb, or a hull whose panels
are developable BY CONSTRUCTION -- a change to the hull-geometry kernel
and to what the ladder floats, not to the unroller. That is why owner and
review_by are unchanged.

work that was done, and the date is clear of the 2026-09-06 pair (Gate 2M,
Gate 2U) and of the 6R/6M cluster so the November rows expire on separate

OWNER chief-architect, UNCHANGED, and now more clearly right: what remains

STALE PROSE CORRECTED 2026-08-13: this entry's metric text cited 97.5 mm for the uncapped fit, now measured 263.3 mm, and its mechanism (b) described the `w**0.15` sheer floor, which the rebuild DELETED. The sheer chord error went 65.6 mm at O(h^0.5) to 8.75 mm at O(h^1.72) and the chine and sheer SWAPPED ROLES: the chine was the well-behaved edge and is now the worse one, because it is no longer a shaping curve but the root of the section quadratic (3.4 -> 10.64 mm chord error at 41 stations).

The last computable count for that family is 21. Any figure quoted for the constant-x edge at 41 stations or above must be a BAND or withdrawn.

It is a partial check, not a proof of stability.
MEASUREMENT CAMPAIGN 2026-08-19, and it relocates the gate's question.
Four results, each measured on the reference hull unless stated:
(1) A C1 SAC FAMILY WAS BUILT AND PROBED (fullness-parameterised
smoothed-power hybrid h=(p+1)s^p - p s^(p+1) and its mirror, flat at
BOTH endpoints for every reachable fullness, closed moments, Cp linear
in the fullnesses; fleet demand verified reachable: 299/300 sampled
designs). It KILLS the x_mb crease (16.3 -> 2.2 mm in [0.5,0.6)) and
moves the bottom 124.0 -> 52.3 mm -- but the topside WORSENS 43.7 ->
57.3 because the flare envelope follows the area curve forward of x_mb,
and neither panel approaches the bar. NOT LANDED: the swap would move
every pinned number and invalidate the Mac's in-flight calibration
corpus for a change that does not cross the bar. Banked in
docs/GATE-6D-DESIGN.md.
(2) TRANSVERSE SEAMS ARE A NULL RESULT: 1, 2 and 3 seam cuts move the
two-sided set metric by < 0.1 mm (bottom 124.04 at every seam count).
The deviation is LOCAL intrinsic twist in the last ~30%, not error
accumulated along the development -- no cutting pattern fixes it.
(3) DIAL ISOLATION: deadrise warp is the bottom's driver (8->30 deg =
52 mm under C1; no warp = 7.9; no warp + no forefoot = 4.1) and flare
is the topside's (flare 0 = 9.4 mm; flare 3 deg alone = 26.8). The
surface at full warp+flare is genuinely non-developable: the gate was
asking a mould hull to be a kit.
(4) THE LOW-TWIST CORNER EXISTS UNDER THE SHIPPED KERNEL: flare = 0,
forefoot = 0, warp <= +8 deg measures 4.6-5.0 mm on BOTH panels --
sharpie/dory-class shapes, the first hulls to pass the bar.

Gate 0E5C-CAP.measured_on: data/e5_chine_warp.json and data/e5_hard_chine_roundtrip.json, from Fridsma R-1275 (DTIC AD0708694, public release) and De Luca & Pensa, Ocean Engineering 139 (2017) Table 1(a,b), CC BY-NC-ND
why_red: THREE MEASURED LIMITS, none of them adjusted to make this pass.
1. NO PARALLEL MIDDLE BODY. A prismatic planing hull has Cp 0.951-0.971.
The genome's box stops at 0.710, and sweeping r_transom and x_mb over
their whole ranges the kernel will not build above Cp 0.848 -- so
lifting the bound would NOT fix it. The sectional-area-curve family is
a power law with exponents in [-6, 8] and cannot hold constant. The
same gap gives Series 60 the worst residual in the E5 corpus (16.6% of
half-beam), from the opposite direction.
2. NO AFT DEADRISE WARP. `beta_len` is bounded at 0.60, so deadrise is
CONSTANT over at least the after 40% of every hull the grammar can
build. Monohedral series fit exactly (Series 62: 0.00 deg). Warped
series do not (NSS 8.27 deg, NTUA 8.69 deg) -- and a warped bottom is
what a developable-panel plywood hull naturally wants, so this is the
form the product is arguably FOR.
3. DEEP-V OUT OF BOX. `beta_mid` stops at 25 deg; Keuning & Alii 1993 is
a 30 deg series. That one is a bound, not a functional form.
THIS IS NOT AN EVIDENCE GAP. The geometry was acquired, it is public
domain, and it is PUBLISHED_PARAMETRIC -- Fridsma Fig. 1 prints the
equations of the chine planform and keel profile, so nothing is digitised
from a drawing. The gate is red because the kernel measurably cannot draw
the hulls, which is the result this gate was built to obtain.
Gate 0E5C-CAP.verify: python scripts/e5_chine_warp.py  (expects 2 of 7 expressible); python -m pytest tests/test_e5_hard_chine.py -q
